Amazing place. Way better than the Matunga south indian restaurants.

Shree Muthappan Eating House is a hidden gem at Bhandup on the Jangal Mangal Road. Appam is the speciality of this place and it is totally worth it. The appam is not the sweet round appam but the Malayalam style Appam like dosa. We also had Sada Dosa which was crispy till the last bite. Sambhar and Chutney are one of the best around Mumbai. Your meal should mandatorily end with filter coffee which has the correct amount of decoction and the required sweetness.

Other specialities are Pazham Pori(Kela Bhajji), Parotta, etc. which we couldn't try.

The hotel is clean and the staff are friendly. Owner is a good person and good to have a conversation with.

You can park your two wheelers outside the restaurant on the road.

The rates are way too economical for the quality of food served.

I would surely visit Muthappan Eating house again.

Cheers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Bhandup Central Restaurant, and while the ambiance was just okay, the standout feature was undoubtedly the non-vegetarian tandoori items.

The decor and atmosphere were quite average, lacking any distinctive flair or charm. The seating was comfortable enough, but the overall environment felt a bit underwhelming. However, what the restaurant lacked in ambiance, it more than made up for with its delicious tandoori offerings.

The tandoori chicken was succulent and perfectly marinated, with just the right amount of spice. Each bite was a delightful explosion of flavors, cooked to perfection in the traditional tandoor oven. The lamb kebabs were equally impressive, tender and juicy with a smoky finish that left a lasting impression. The variety of tandoori dishes available catered to different palates, ensuring there was something for everyone to enjoy.

The service was efficient, and the staff were friendly and attentive, making sure our dining experience was pleasant despite the unremarkable surroundings.

In conclusion, Bhandup Central Restaurant may not win any awards for its ambiance, but it is definitely worth a visit for its excellent non-vegetarian tandoori items. If you're a fan of well-cooked, flavorful tandoori dishes, this place won't disappoint.

featured_reviews.review_text:
During my multiple visits to this hotel, I have observed that they use Delicious Fat Spread instead of real butter in their food. While butter is a dairy product made from milk,Delicious Fat Spread is made from vegetable oils, and the two have very different properties.

Although Delicious Fat Spread is also manufactured by Amul and marketed as a versatile alternative to butter, it is not the same as real Amul Butter. When I asked the hotel staff about it, they claimed they use Amul Butter — but in reality, they use Delicious Fat Spread.

This product may not be as healthy as real butter, especially for those who prefer natural dairy products. My only intention in sharing this review is to make people aware: if you order dishes here that contain butter, you may actually be served fat spread instead.

Please choose your food carefully and stay healthy.
Eat healthy, stay healthy.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mitran Da Dhaba is an amazing place if you love authentic Punjabi dhaba-style tandoor food. This is a complete dhaba experience, so I’d strongly recommend ordering their tandoor specials, parathas, and even Chinese dishes rather than Mughlai or biryanis.

The place has an open-space setup, which feels great when you’re dining with friends or family. Everything is very clean and hygienically prepared, and it really feels like there are specialized chefs handling specific dishes — the taste clearly reflects their expertise. Portions are very generous, so you definitely get good value for money.

All tandoori dishes are outstanding and cooked live in front of you, which adds to the experience. Must-try items include Reshmi Kebab, Kheema Paratha, Chicken Fried Rice, White Makhan Tandoori Chicken, and of course the Gulab Jamuns, which are absolutely amazing.

Parking is convenient — you can park your car or bike on the opposite side of the road, and since there’s usually no traffic jam after 8 PM, it’s quite hassle-free. Do note that menu prices are exclusive of GST, so factor that in while ordering.

Weekends can get crowded, but weekday evenings are comfortable and much less busy, making it a perfect time for a relaxed dinner.

Overall, a must-visit dhaba for tandoor lovers! 🔥🍗

featured_reviews.name: Prasad K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bhau Vada Pav – A Bhandup Classic

Bhau Vada Pav is easily one of the best spots in Bhandup for vada pav—and that’s not just nostalgia talking. I’ve been eating here since childhood. It used to be just around the corner from my school, and I’d treat myself to a vada pav every now and then. Decades later, not much has changed, and that’s a good thing.

Their vada pav has always been slightly more expensive than other stalls, but it’s worth every rupee. The quality stands out. The vada is large, crispy on the outside, soft inside, and full of flavor. It’s sandwiched in a generously sized pav with their signature red garlic chutney, plus a couple of fried green chilies on the side. Best eaten hot—when the flavors really come alive.

Even today, the quality is exactly how I remember it. That kind of consistency is rare.

They do offer other snacks, but honestly, I’ve never felt the need to try anything beyond the vada pav—it’s that good. The shop is usually crowded, with no seating. You either stand inside and eat or get it packed to go.

If you’re in Bhandup and haven’t had Bhau’s vada pav, you’re missing out. It’s a must-try.

featured_reviews.review_text:
"I traveled from very far specifically to visit Rekdee - Taste of the Streets in Mulund for their late night food. The experience was a masterclass in how inconsistent management and staff can drive away genuine customers.

The Logical Contradiction:
Upon arrival, the boy at the counter informed me that Misal Pav was not available, but Tari Pav was. When I questioned the logic—given that both dishes share the exact same Tari (curry) and Pav—he failed to provide a valid reason. He then claimed a specific '12 AM to 4 AM' rule where Misal Pav is simply not served. I initially accepted this as a business policy maybe thinking that tarri pav has more profit and it consumes less tari as compared to a misal so they can make around 4-5 tari pavs instead of making 1 misal for profit, choosing to be reasonable and patient.

The Blatant Bias:
The situation changed 10 minutes later when a different family arrived. It was clear the management was partial to this specific group. Suddenly, the '12 AM to 4 AM' rule vanished, and the same staff member announced he was taking 'last orders' for Misal Pav for them. When confronted, he shamelessly claimed the Misal had 'magically' come back into stock. Only after being caught in this lie did he dismissively say, 'If you want now, we can give you,' which entirely missed the point of my concern regarding fair treatment.

The Linguistic Insult & Cowardice:
When I advised the staff that rules should be consistent for everyone, the boy cowardly hid behind the owner, claiming he was just following orders—despite being the one who originally gave me the 'lecture.' To make matters worse, both the owner and the boy began speaking in Gujarati, assuming I wouldn't understand their comments about a 'mess being created.' They were visibly stunned when I informed them that I understood every word of their mockery.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavours That Truly Impress – Must-Try Spot in Bhandup!

Tried Udupi 2 Mumbai in Bhandup and was genuinely blown away by the taste and quality. I ordered the Hara Bhara Kebab and Veg Schezwan Noodles, and both dishes were nothing short of fantastic.

The Hara Bhara Kebabs were crisp on the outside, soft and well-seasoned inside—served piping hot with a chutney that perfectly complemented the flavors. A great start to the meal!

But the highlight? The Veg Schezwan Noodles—packed with bold flavors, just the right spice level, and loaded with fresh veggies. It had that perfect street-style touch while still feeling clean and well-balanced.

The restaurant has a simple yet pleasant ambiance, and the service was prompt and polite. It’s the kind of place where the food speaks louder than the decor—and that’s a good thing!

If you’re in or around Bhandup and love flavorful veg food, Udupi 2 Mumbai is a must-visit. Already planning my next order!

featured_reviews.name: Prasad K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Udupi 2 Mumbai on LBS Road, Bhandup, and it turned out to be an amazing vegetarian restaurant experience. They have ground-floor seating (non-AC) and a first floor with air-conditioned seating. The overall vibe is good, but the first floor is definitely the standout — really comfortable and pleasant.

It’s a pure vegetarian place with a strong South Indian menu: idli, dosa, medu wada, appam and many other varieties — all delicious. They also serve full North Indian meals.

I visited for lunch and we started with paneer spring rolls — had them after ages and it took me straight back to childhood. They were excellent. Then we tried paneer angara with tandoori roti, paneer pahadi kebab, and paneer tikka biryani — yes, complete paneer overload, but everything tasted great. Paneer angara was the highlight for me.
Only disappointment — they don’t serve roomali roti.

The sweet lime soda was a letdown (no fizz, no ice), but apart from that the food was fantastic.
Service was amazing throughout — the staff was attentive, friendly, and very helpful. They even have special seating arrangements for small kids.

Overall, loved the vibe and would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
Two areas of improvement would be allowing customers to choose two different mocktails under the offer, especially since all mocktails are priced the same.

Another thing to improve is the coordination between staff members—there was a noticeable communication gap while placing our order.

Visited The Food Studio near Nahur Railway Station and had a generally pleasant experience. We were seated within 5 minutes, and the ambiance was nice with a large TV setup in the center, adding a lively vibe to the place.

We started with French fries and a few starters: Jhinga Koliwada, Makhmali Kumbh, Pomfret Tandoori, and Chicken Burnt Garlic. The Jhinga Koliwada was the highlight—crispy and flavorful. Makhmali Kumbh is a great vegetarian option, stuffed with cheese and tasted quite good. However, the Pomfret Tandoori didn’t meet expectations—the masala lacked punch.

For the main course, we ordered Sabzi Peshawari with roti. It leaned towards the sweeter side, possibly due to the mix of paneer, mushrooms, and green peas. Not bad if you enjoy mildly sweet gravies.

We also tried the mocktail Mulokai under their Buy 1 Get 1 Free offer. The taste was average.

Overall, a good experience with room for a few improvements.
